decisions.reason: Requiring labels on every interactive field and specifying their design does not change the existing Danish-language or placeholder-text values.
Label coverage and design do not change the requirement to preserve Title-field formatting during interaction.
The source adds label coverage and a label-design reference but does not alter the field implementation mechanism or robustness architecture.
Adding labels to interactive fields does not change how placeholder text must clear when a field is activated.
The label instruction does not explicitly replace, resolve, or modify the separate unresolved requirement concerning grey editable-field cues.
The source does not change the date field's calendar-dropdown entry method; its label is governed by the source requirement.
The label instruction does not alter the checklist-and-dropdown control configuration.
Interactive-field labels are unrelated to Tab-driven list hierarchy and alignment behavior.
The source specifies control-label coverage and design but does not necessarily change the existing complete style-catalog requirement.
The control-label design reference does not modify graphic bullet sizing, alignment, scaling, appearance, or color.
Interactive control labels are distinct from image and table captions, so the caption targets, typography, and style name remain unchanged.
The instruction concerning interactive-field labels does not change the requirement to include the required theme colors.
